title: Capacity bridge & geography acceleration — BlueMarlin check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on stepping up committed capacity, adding EU region routing, and lining up a short private VPC pilot. Customer has steady growth (30% q/q token growth), tight 99th percentile latency targets for inference, and an upcoming procurement approval window in mid-January. Action items include benchmark runs, pricing addendum, and SOC2/KMS docs to unblock procurement.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted for EU routing
Timeline for contract extension and pilot
next_steps: Send 12-month extension pricing addendum with +40% capacity tier and pro-rated billing options (Grace) — by 2026-12-21
SE to run 99th perc latency baseline on 16B model across us-west & eu-west (Ethan) — results by 2026-12-22
Share SOC2 Type II report and KMS integration guide (Priya) — today 2026-12-17
Schedule VPC private pilot kickoff for week of 2027-01-04 (Grace + Maya)
action_items: Ethan Novak (SE): Run perf benchmark: 16B model, 4k context, 80 RPS sustained, capture p50/p95/p99 and memory/KV cache metrics — due 2026-12-22
Grace Park (AE): Prepare pricing addendum with option A (12mo +40%), option B (6mo +20%), include overage terms — due 2026-12-21
Priya Rao (CSM): Attach SOC2 report, KMS/HSM integration notes, and link to audit log export docs to this thread — due 2026-12-17 (EOD)
Maya Singh (Customer): Confirm primary EU data residency requirement and stakeholder list for procurement — due 2026-12-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-17 14:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Grace, Ethan, Priya (Redwood); Maya, Carlos, Leah, Omar (BlueMarlin)

Summary (auto): Quick renewal and expansion sync. BlueMarlin wants more committed capacity and an EU routing footprint; procurement needs security docs. SE asked for perf baselines to validate latency at current model sizes.

[00:00] Grace (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on — hope the timing's good. quick agenda: usage recap, capacity options, eu routing/private pilot, procurement docs, then wrap with next steps.
[00:17] Maya (BlueMarlin): Yep, thanks. timing's fine. we've seen steady growth — tokens are up about 30% q over q since Sept, and we hit a few 99th latency spikes last month during nightly batch inference.
[00:31] Ethan (Redwood SE): Can you remind me which models you're serving in prod? last time you mentioned 13B and 70B variants?
[00:39] Maya: Yeah, primarily a 16B variant derived from an open model — we call it internal "marlin-16"; sometimes fall back to a trimmed 7B for low latency paths. 70B is more experimental in staging. the 16B is the one producing the spikes at 95–99.
[00:53] Carlos (CTO): And the 99th has to be less than 220ms for interactive flows; otherwise UX ops notices it. there's some wiggle room for batch.
[01:05] Grace: Got it. on the capacity side, you previously had a committed pool in us-west; you're asking to scale that by roughly 40% and add eu-west routing for EU customers — is that the scope?
[01:18] Maya: yes, exactly. we want the committed uplift, plus the ability to route EU traffic to a eu region for residency and lower latency. ideally a dedicated pool or private option for eu because of residency requirements.
[01:31] Leah (SRE): just to add — we run p99 checks every hour. the failures correlate with bursts when multiple batches hit concurrently. curious if Redwood's batching and KV cache policies could be tuned without doubling cost.
[01:45] Ethan: yeah there's a couple levers. continuous batching windows, dynamic batch size caps, and prefix/K V cache tuning — sometimes the K V cash doesn't warm fast enough. also quantization profiles can reduce cost but might change accuracy — we can show tradeoffs.
[02:04] Maya: K V cash? did you mean KV cache? sometimes the transcripts scramble abbreviations.
[02:09] Ethan: sorry yes, KV cache, but my brain says K V cash apparently.
[02:14] Carlos: ha. the important part is whether we hit the 220ms p99 target. if dedicated EU nodes will do that, procurement prefers we go dedicated + VPC.
[02:26] Grace: procurement angle — Omar, any specifics from procurement that block renewal?
[02:30] Omar (Procurement): Mainly SOC2 evidence, KMS key management integration (we use an on-prem HSM), and contract terms for data residency and audit logs. Also price clarity for commit levels and overages.
[02:44] Priya (CSM): we can send the SOC2 Type II and our KMS integration guide. for HSM we have options: customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or bring-your-own-HSM over a VPC tunnel — we should detail that in the docs.
[02:58] Maya: perfect. also need to see how logs are exported — retention windows and whether logs contain payloads or only metadata.
[03:07] Ethan: logs export can be metadata-only by default; full audit exports are available for dedicated/private setups. we'll mark that in the write-up.
[03:15] Carlos: about cost/latency tradeoff, can Redwood run a quick proof-of-performance so we can present numbers to finance? baseline p50/p95/p99 plus cost per 1k tokens?
[03:27] Grace: yes. Ethan can run a benchmark on our infra — we'll scope the RPS and the model.
[03:33] Ethan: I'll schedule runs for 80 RPS sustained on the 16B with 4k context, and capture p50/p95/p99. i'll also collect KV cache hit rates and memory footprints.
[03:46] Leah: do you need us to open any firewall or test keys for the VPC pilot?
[03:50] Ethan: for a private VPC pilot we'll need a short period of connectivity and a service account with role limited access. we'll share a checklist.
[03:58] Maya: timeline — procurement meeting is Jan 12th, they'd like numbers and security package before then.
[04:03] Grace: so we have an internal target: final proposal in hand by Dec 21st to allow time for approvals. does that sound realistic?
[04:10] Omar: yes that helps. pricing addendum by Dec 21st would let us present at the Jan 12th procurement window.
[04:17] Priya: i'll attach SOC2 + KMS guide to the thread today. Grace, we'll also put a note about audit log exports and retention policies.
[04:24] Grace: perfect. a couple of technical clarifications: when you say dedicated EU nodes, do you need racks on your own private redwood pool or would a Dedicated (reserved) eu pool suffice?
[04:36] Maya: reserved pool is fine as long as the data never leaves EU and keys are customer-controlled. we don't require on-prem hardware for inference, just residency and key control.
[04:46] Ethan: that matches what Dedicated offers — dedicated GPU pools with VPC peering and customer KMS options. we'll list the options A/B in the addendum.
[04:56] Carlos: any competitors we should be aware of offering cheaper eu-only endpoints? we've had a vendor mention LambdaEdge offering a region-only discount.
[05:05] Grace: noted — we'll include competitor positioning. but the differentiator here is the observability (token-level cost breakdown and rollouts) which you mentioned helps with cost controls.
[05:16] Maya: yes, their retention+tracing has helped us catch regressions. one ask: can Redwood tie regression alerts to prompt sets?
[05:24] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize can link evals and prompts to alert on quality regressions — we'll share the docs on how to set that up.
[05:33] Ethan: quick note from the bench — quantization to int8 helped similar customers reduce token cost by ~28% but there was a small delta in NLU scores; we can include a recommended quantization profile for marlin-16.
[05:47] Leah: okay great. for the pilot, we'll want to validate both latency and correctness (a small eval set).
[05:55] Grace: agreed. proposed pilot: two-week VPC pilot in eu-west with 50% production traffic shadowed, perf metrics + eval set. if that validates, roll to dedicated EU pool and apply the commit.
[06:08] Maya: sounds reasonable. who owns the pilot runbook?
[06:11] Ethan: Redwood SE will lead the runbook; BlueMarlin will provide evals and access. we'll produce a checklist and measurement plan.
[06:19] Grace: ok wrapping: recap of next steps — Grace to send pricing addendum; Priya SOC2 + KMS docs; Ethan perf runs; schedule pilot kickoff first week of Jan.
[06:32] Omar: i'll coordinate procurement and forward any legal must-haves.
[06:36] Maya: thanks. one last question — can you indicate SLA targets for p99 after we commit? we need an SLA number to show procurement.
[06:44] Grace: committed SLA for p99 under Dedicated is available as an add-on; we'll outline options in the addendum (target values and credits).
[06:52] Carlos: awesome. thanks team.
[06:55] Grace: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains a few abbreviations mis-heard (KV cache as K V cash) and occasional speaker overlaps. This export is intended as a meeting artifact and not an exact verbatim record.
